remove: The pale specular dashes and highlight edges in the key-plate grain. At actual size they read as a digital bevel or scratched-vinyl effect, not wood type, and they are the noisiest thing on a page that otherwise runs on restraint.
top_problem: The big idea is ref-02 panel 4, a cropped vertical CANTINA on the right with red tracked section heads, rebuilt in tidier type. The Iowa City fusion (print-town letterpress) lives only in proposal.md, so it fails the §5 substitution test: any cantina in any city could print this sheet. The boldest missing idea is a gesture where Mexico and Iowa City are fused in the image itself, not claimed in the rationale. The letterforms also read as collegiate athletic block, not rótulo.
fixes: Make the register slip unmistakable. At full size the red still escapes mostly on the left and bottom edges of every letter from the first N down, so it reads as an offset drop shadow. Double the rotation, or add a visible second-colour misregistration inside the counters, so the red visibly changes sides along the word.

Give the concept an ownable Iowa City and Mexico fusion that a guest can see (for example, cut the monument from a specific rótulo alphabet rather than a block grotesk, and let the plate carry a real Iowa City press artefact such as a type-case or broadside rule system). Without it criterion 15 cannot pass 60.

Kill the dead islands. Cut the section gap from 5 rows to 3 and redistribute, or widen col1 toward the monument, so the right column is not four floating clusters with a 110 px hole at Cider. Then equalise top and bottom margins (currently 122 vs 76 px).
Replace the streaky feTurbulence grain with a coarser, lower-contrast wood grain that shows no light highlights, and check it at 100% print size so it reads as ink starvation, not vertical scratches.

Rebalance weight. The centroid sits at x 0.81 and the left column carries no counter-mass, so give the section heads a slightly larger size (for example 17 px) or pull the list 1-2 rows higher so the reading layer answers the monument instead of floating beside it.

lens: items and prices vs draft_doc rev 3; ingredient names and description completeness (public_components); menu flow for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The menu is honest but half-written. Four cocktails get full ingredient lines, and the other ten items fall back to placeholder copy that repeats the item name ('Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour', 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Dry red wine'). In a Mexican cantina the agave pours are the house's calling card, yet they are the thinnest lines on the page. Five-row pacing gaps also turn the list into scattered islands instead of a reading path.
problems: Prices: all 14 items and all 14 prices match draft_doc exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13). No item was invented or dropped.

The order within Classics changed without a note. The draft has Manhattan then Margarita; the design prints Margarita then Manhattan. It is defensible for a cantina, but proposal.md does not declare it.
The Manhattan correctly hides aromatic bitters (public_components false). Its line 'Rye whiskey · sweet vermouth · cocktail cherry' is complete for what may be shown.

The garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel, cocktail cherry) do not appear in draft_doc components except the cherry. The proposal sources them to phg.recipe_versions.garnish (gateway log 213). I could not verify this in my lens, so the accuracy reviewer must confirm it or content_integrity flips to fail.

Descriptions for the spirits, beers, wines and cider are the draft's placeholder strings copied verbatim. Missing ABV, region and brand data is a known gap (awaiting_owner_data) and not the designer's fault. But 'Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour' and 'VSOP Cognac pour' simply repeat the item name, and 'Hop-forward draft IPA' is taxonomy wording. The page prints no visible flag for missing data.
The naming is inconsistent: the item 'Blanco Tequila' sits beside the Margarita's ingredient 'Tequila blanco'. Pick one order.

Flow: the columns run Cocktails → Spirits | Beer → Cider → Wine. Agave next to cocktails suits a cantina. But section heads paired across columns (Cocktails/Beer, Spirits/Wine) invite a row-wise Z-read that competes with the column-wise path. Cider floats alone mid-column, and Cognac VSOP is stranded at the bottom after a 5-row gap.
Pacing gaps of 3 to 5 empty rows (for example Manhattan → House Originals, Añejo → Brandy, Amber Lager → Cider) read as holes, not grouping. The page is filled by air, not by content.
The venue name 'CANTINA' in the monument is not in draft_doc (title 'Bar menu'). The proposal does not source it; confirm it is the venue's real name.

Price format is consistent: inline, no $, whole numbers, tabular figures, muted ink, maximum eye travel 7.9%. The muted INK2 prices are quieter than the names, a choice that makes scanning prices slightly harder in dim bar light.
Taglines and captions: there are none. The foot line '& Cocktail Bar / Iowa City, Iowa' is a venue fact from the brief, not an item fact. Pass.
fixes: Rewrite the spirit lines from known facts so they do not repeat the item name (for example 'Unaged, 100% agave' only if sourced; otherwise 'Neat or on the rocks' as a serve line), and print an unobtrusive 'details to come' or keep a flagged placeholder until Rob supplies the brands, ABV and regions.

Cut the section gap from 5 rows to 2 or 3 and the sub-head gap from 3 rows to 2, then use the recovered rows to bring Cider up under Beer and keep Brandy with Agave, so each column reads as one continuous path.
Stagger or offset the section-head rows between columns (do not force Cocktails/Beer and Spirits/Wine onto shared rows) so the eye reads down column 1 and then column 2 instead of Z-scanning.
Restore the draft order in Classics (Manhattan, Margarita), or record the swap and its reason in proposal.md, and align 'Tequila blanco' / 'Blanco Tequila' naming.
Add the source (input or Supabase row) for the venue name 'CANTINA' and each garnish to proposal.md so the content gate can be verified without a lookup.

lens: Checked every printed ingredient, garnish and label against build/draft_doc.json (rev 3) and phg.recipe_versions via gateway log_id 218. Checked how descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png and preview-phone.png.
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to a source, but the facts are thin. The Margarita garnish 'lime wheel' comes from recipe_version f06abb74, the House Daiquiri 'lime coin' from 14d45e57, the Manhattan 'cocktail cherry' from 9fb77eaa and the Old Fashioned 'orange peel' from 7095fd3d. The Manhattan's aromatic bitters are rightly hidden because public_components aromatic-bitters is false, and the accents in Añejo and Rosé match the source. The problem is criterion 12: 'Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour' and 'VSOP Cognac pour' only repeat the item name, and 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine' and 'Hop-forward draft IPA' read like database classes, which is the automatic-fail condition. The voice is also split: three cocktails are bare lists separated by dots, while the Margarita alone ends in a tasting sentence. For a Mexican cantina the list reads generic. The Margarita and two tequilas are the only Mexican content against a Manhattan, an Old Fashioned, a Czech Pilsner, a Malbec, a Pinot Grigio and a Cognac. There is no mezcal, no Mexican beer and no Spanish section wording, so only the CANTINA wordmark carries the venue.
fixes: Rewrite the six name-repeating or class-label descriptions in guest language using only verified facts; the known ABV, region and brand gap (awaiting_owner_data, not penalised) means asking Rob for tasting notes or producers rather than printing 'X pour'. Examples of verified facts: the draft desc 'Crisp pale lager.' and the agave category.

Pick one voice for every cocktail: either all dot-lists with no closing sentence, or all four with a short sensory line built only from their recipe_version components. The Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' (from the draft desc) is currently the only one.

Label pours: 'By the Glass' covers Malbec and Pinot Grigio, but the Brut Rosé 13 under 'Sparkling' and the three spirits at 12, 16 and 18 have no glass or pour label; add a label such as 'glass' or '1.5 oz' once the draft or Rob supplies the pour size, since none is in the source now.

Venue fit: send a note to the Coordinator and Rob that the list lacks the categories a Mexican cantina guest expects (mezcal, Mexican lager, agua fresca or other non-alcoholic drinks). Also consider Spanish sub-head wording from the source, such as 'Agave' kept and 'Tequila' pours grouped with the cocktails first. Separately, phg.menu_items still holds 'Junmai Ginjo' $12 (log 218), which draft rev 3 omits; confirm the draft is the intended source.

Layout note for the designer: the 22 px description leading makes two-line descriptions read as double-spaced. The letter version also breaks the House Daiquiri after 'fresh lime juice ·' at about half the column measure, while the Old Fashioned runs full width. Tighten the description leading to about 17 px and use one consistent measure.
